thread:
kevin: Anyone else seeing a weird p95 jump on /v1/generate when requests fan out to the exit-node? p50 is unchanged. chart: https://redwood.internal/charts/abc123 :eyes:
anya: Hmm can you paste the query you ran? which route and exit-node?
kevin: query: `/v1/generate?route=experimental-fanout&exit_node=eu-west-1`
sofia: could be sampling origin mismatch. Console sometimes shows p50 from edge and p95 from exit-node after rollouts. Did we change route-weighting recently?
jamal: also check whether the metric is `service_latency_ms` vs `client_latency_ms` — one measures post-fanout, the other includes gateway queuing. p95 can diverge if they get mixed.
platform-bot: Routing policy update deployed by @deploy-bot at 1754443000 — rollout experimental-fanout: 50% -> 70% (note: gradual)
anya: ok that timing aligns. On the telemetry side we tag samples with `sample_origin: edge|exit-node|gateway`. Are those tags present in the rollup query?
kevin: looked at traces, saw disproportionate tail at the exit-node. sample of spans: `exit-node.process  p95=420ms p50=90ms` vs `edge.proxy p95=110ms p50=60ms`
sofia: that points to backend variability. But console behavior still suspicious — the latency widget's legend says "percentile by route" but I think it uses the rollup key `route_rollup=true` which collapses exit-node tags. It can mix origins during merges.
jamal: can we quickly pin the route-weighting to single-exit variant for the canary and compare? if p95 drops, it's rollout-induced. Otherwise it's an exit-node perf issue.
kevin: I'll spin a short-lived canary with `route=experimental-fanout&exit_node=single-eu` and post results in 10m.
anya: i'll open a console bug: dashboard should surface `sample_origin` filter for percentile calc. short note: "percentiles must be computed per-origin or explicitly labeled as mixed"
platform-bot: SLO alert fired: generate.p95 > 200ms in eu-west-1 (1754443460)
jamal: FYI quota/backpressure could amplify tails — if downstream is slow, retries add skew. Check `retry_attempts` and `quota_throttled` counters for the window.
sofia: for short term, suggest dashboard change: show small table: p50/p95 per `sample_origin` alongside rollup. longer term, ensure rollup preserves origin provenance.
kevin: confirmed canary numbers: p95 -> 130ms on single-eu vs 380ms on fanout. looks rollout + exit-node combo. I'll keep canary running and file an ops ticket to reduce rollout to 30% until exit-node patch.
anya: thanks — I'll link the dashboard ticket to the rollout and add a note to the runbook about mixing origins.
jamal: i'll run a small synthetic load against exit-node to reproduce and share flamegraphs. ping if you want me to pause the rollout sooner. :thumbsup:
